newsitem.title: USA: PepsiCo spin-off not to affect dividend.
newsitem.headline: PepsiCo spin-off not to affect dividend.

text.p: PepsiCo Inc chairman Roger Enrico told shareholders at the company's annual meeting on Wednesday that the planned spin-off of its restaurant business will not result in lower PepsiCo dividends.
PepsiCo on Wednesday raised its quarterly dividend $0.01 to $0.125 per share.

PepsiCo in January announced plans to spin off KFC, Pizza Hut and Taco Bell to shareholders as a separate company later this year. Restaurants supplied 36 percent of PepsiCo's $31.65 billion in 1996 sales.
"You won't be seeing a reduction in the dividend on the Pepsi side," Enrico said.
Enrico said the total cost of the spin-off would be about $50 million. A PepsiCo spokesman later said these costs would not have an impact on earnings.

Enrico said the spin-off was a response to a more competitive marketplace, which requires management teams that focus on either the restaurant business or the beverage and snack-food business, but not both.
"The world has changed," Enrico said. "It's become a lot more competitive. And we need to change, too."
PepsiCo shares closed at 36, down 1/2 on the day.
